prerequisites: Basic notions acquired in previous Physics and Mathematics courses

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics and fields and waves.
Know the basic instrumentation to measure physical quantities.
Know the basic techniques for evaluating experimental data.
Develop practical solutions to elementary technical engineering problems in the fields of mechanics and fields and waves.

syllabus_topics: UNITS, PHYSICAL QUANTITIES AND VECTORS: The nature of Physics. Consistency and unit conversions. Uncertainty and significant figures. Estimates and orders of magnitude. Vectors and vector addition. Vector components. Unit vectors. Vector products. Sliding Vectors

KINEMATICS OF THE POINT: Position, velocity and acceleration vectors. Mean and instantaneous values. Angular velocity and angular acceleration vectors. Mean and instantaneous values. Relationship between linear and angular kinematic magnitudes. Intrinsic Components. Study of simple movements: rectilinear motion, circular motion, oblique projectile motion. Expressions of kinematic magnitudes in Cartesian and polar coordinates

NEWTON'S LAWS OF MOTION: Force and interactions. Newton's first law. Inertial and non-inertial reference frames. Newton's second law. Mass and weight. Newton's third law. Momentum. Mechanical impulse. Angular momentum. Contact forces: active, constraint.

WORK AND KINETIC ENERGY: Work done by a force. Power. Kinetic energy. Conservative and non-conservative forces. Elastic potential energy. Potential energy in the gravitational field. Mechanical energy. Force and potential energy. Principle of conservation of mechanical energy.

KINEMATICS OF POINT SYSTEMS: System of points. Rigid body. Translation motion. Rotation motion around a fixed axis. General or roto-translational motion. Instantaneous center of rotation. Rolling. Relative motion.

DYNAMICS OF PARTICLE SYSTEMS: Particle systems. Internal and external forces. Center of mass of the system. Motion of the center of mass. Equations of motion of a particle system. Linear momentum. Conservation theorem. Angular momentum of a particle system. Conservation theorem. Work and power. Potential and kinetic energy of a particle system. Energy theorem of a particle system. Collisions.

DYNAMICS OF THE RIGID BODY: Rotation of a rigid body around a fixed axis. Moments and products of inertia. Calculation of moments of inertia. Steiner's theorem. Moment of a force and couple of forces. Equations of general rigid body motion. Kinetic energy in general rigid body motion. Work in general rigid body motion. Angular momentum of a rigid body. Conservation theorem.
STATICS: Equilibrium of rigid bodies. Center of gravity. Stability. Degrees of freedom and constraints

PERIODIC MOTION: Description of oscillation. Simple harmonic motion. Energy in simple harmonic motion. Applications of simple harmonic motion. The simple pendulum. The physical pendulum. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations and resonance.
FLUID MECHANICS: Density. Pressure in a fluid. Fundamental principles of Fluidostatics. Continuity equation. Bernoulli's equation.

MECHANICAL WAVES: Types of mechanical waves. Periodic waves. Mathematical description of a wave. Speed of a transverse wave. Energy of wave motion. Wave interference, boundary conditions and superposition. Standing waves on a string. Normal modes of a string.

LABORATORY: Theory of Measurements, Errors, Graphs and Fits. Examples. Reaction Time. Determination of the density of a body. Relative Motion. Instantaneous velocity. Study of the Simple Pendulum. Experiments with a helical spring. Damped and forced oscillations. Moments of inertia. Determination of the radius of gyration of a body. Standing waves.

UNSTRUCTURED LABORATORY: Sessions with unstructured activities (open practice) covering the theoretical content of the practices listed above. Student groups must solve a practical problem proposed by the teacher, selecting the theoretical framework and experimental tools to obtain the solution; for this, they will have basic information and teacher guidance.

assessment_methods.method: Practical report, practicum and external internships report

assessment_rules: The final grade (G) is calculated as 40% from continuous assessment (C), 40% from a final exam (F), and 20% from laboratory work (L). Students must achieve a final grade of 5.0 or higher out of 10 to pass the course. Opportunities are provided to replace earlier C, F, or L grades with new ones. Unethical behavior, such as copying or using unauthorized electronic devices, will result in a failing grade of 0.0 for that evaluation opportunity.
